reading.body:
College Board appears in this data with one product, BigFuture, and no verified AI features.

The pattern is a large education nonprofit whose only listed AI-category product is a free college and career planning tool for high school students and families. The data records its age gates and privacy policy but not what the product does with AI, so the classification rests on the category label rather than on any confirmed capability.

For AI specifically, this matters as a boundary case. BigFuture is a planning and scholarship tool, not a compute-intensive system, and nothing in the data ties it to data centers, power demand, or model training. If AI is present, it is likely embedded in a consumer product rather than driving infrastructure.

What the data does not cover is substantial. There are no lawsuits, SEC filings, patents, or MCP servers listed, and no AI features are verified. A reader should treat this as a record of a product and its access rules, not as evidence about how much compute College Board uses or buys.

profile_text.body:
College Board operates BigFuture, a free college and career planning site at bigfuture.collegeboard.org. According to the site, it lets students compare colleges, explore career possibilities, and learn about financial aid and scholarships. It also offers a BigFuture Community Library with hundreds of videos and articles covering topics from college applications to scholarships to SAT prep, and a scholarship drawing that the site says has no essay, no minimum GPA, and no test score requirements. The site cites research finding that less than half of first-year college students completely agree their college is a good fit, and frames its guidance around helping students find that fit.

BigFuture is listed as an Education and Research AI product. Its AI features are not verified. The site describes its audience as high school students and families, with College Board accounts for ages 13 and up, a parent consent form required under 13, and the BigFuture School app available to ages 13 and up through school agreements. It is free and governed by the College Board privacy policy. No lawsuits, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for the company.
